quinze: A game at cards in which the object is to make fifteen points.
questorship: The office, or the term of office, of a questor.
quadrivalent: Having a valence of four; capable of combining with, being replaced by, or compared with, four monad atoms; tetravalent; -- said of certain atoms and radicals; thus, carbon and silicon are quadrivalent elements.
quintile: The aspect of planets when separated the fifth part of the zodiac, or 72º. Hutton.
questionability: The state or condition of being questionable. Stallo.
quirked: Having, or formed with, a quirk or quirks.
quamoclit: Formerly, a genus of plants including the cypress vine (Quamoclit vulgaris, now called Ipomoea Quamoclit). The genus is now merged in Ipomoea.
quadrennial: 1. Comprising four years; as, a quadrennial period. 2. Occurring once in four years, or at the end of every four years; as, quadrennial games.
quotation: 1. The act of quoting or citing. 2. That which is quoted or cited; a part of a book or writing named, repeated, or adduced as evidence or illustration. Locke. 3. (Com.) The naming or publishing of the current price of stocks, bonds, or any commodity; also the price named. 4. Quota; share. (old) 5.
quatercousin: A cousin within the first four degrees of kindred.
quiritation: A crying for help. (old) Bp. Hall.
quattrocento: The fifteenth century, when applied to Italian art or literature; as, the sculpture of the quattrocento; quattrocento style. --Quat`tro*cen"tist (#), n.
quinquefid: Sharply cut about halfway to the middle or base into five segments; as, a quinquefid leaf or corolla.
quindecemvir: One of a sacerdotal college of fifteen men whose chief duty was to take care of the Sibylline books.
quebracho: A Chilian apocynaceous tree (Aspidosperma Quebracho); also, its bark, which is used as a febrifuge, and for dyspnoea of the lung, or bronchial diseases; -- called also white quebracho, to distinguish it from the red quebracho, a Mexican anacardiaceous tree (Loxopterygium Lorentzii) whose bark is said to have similar properties. J. Smith (Dict. Econ. Plants).
quilting: 1. The act of stitching or running in patterns, as in making a quilt. 2. A quilting bee. See Bee, 2. 3. The material used for making quilts. 4. (Naut.) A coating of strands of rope for a water vessel.
quas: A kind of beer. Same as Quass.
quirinal: Of, pertaining to, or designating, the hill Collis Quirinalis, now Monte Quirinale (one of the seven hills of Rome), or a modern royal place situated upon it. Also used substantively.
quahaug: An American market clam (Venus mercenaria). It is sold in large quantities, and is highly valued as food. Called also round clam, and hard clam. Note: The name is also applied to other allied species, as Venus Mortoni of the Gulf of Mexico.
quech: A word occurring in a corrupt passage of Bacon's Essays, and probably meaning, to stir, to move.
quartan: Of or pertaining to the fourth; occurring every fourth day, reckoning inclusively; as, a quartan ague, or fever. | 1. (Med.) An intermittent fever which returns every fourth day, reckoning inclusively, that is, one in which the interval between paroxysms is two days. 2. A measure, the fourth part of some other…
quinogen: A hypothetical radical of quinine and related alkaloids.
quoll: A marsupial of Australia (Dasyurus macrurus), about the size of a cat.
quarry: Same as 1st Quarrel. (old) Fairfax. | 1. (a) A part of the entrails of the beast taken, given to the hounds. (b) A heap of game killed. 2. The object of the chase; the animal hunted for; game; especially, the game hunted with hawks.
quahog: An American market clam (Venus mercenaria). It is sold in large quantities, and is highly valued as food. Called also round clam, and hard clam. Note: The name is also applied to other allied species, as Venus Mortoni of the Gulf of Mexico.
quab: An unfledged bird; hence, something immature or unfinished. Ford.
quadra: (a) The plinth, or lowest member, of any pedestal, podium, water table, or the like. (b) A fillet, or listel.
quarreling: Engaged in a quarrel; apt or disposed to quarrel; as, quarreling factions; a quarreling mood. -- Quar"rel*ing*ly, adv.
quintessence: 1. The fifth or last and highest essence or power in a natural body. See Ferment oils, under Ferment. (old) Note: The ancient Greeks recognized four elements, fire, air, water, and earth. | To distil or extract as a quintessence; to reduce to a quintessence. Stirling. "Truth quintessenced and raised to the highest power." J. A. Symonds.
quorum: Such a number of the officers or members of any body as is competent by law or constitution to transact business; as, a quorum of the House of Representatives; a constitutional quorum was not present. Note: The term arose from the Latin words, Quorum aliquem vestrum . . .
quits: See the Note under Quit, a.
quadrigeminal: Fourfold; having four similar parts, or two pairs of similar parts. Quadrigeminal bodies (Anat.), two pairs of lobes, or elevations, on the dorsal side of the midbrain of most mammals; the optic lobes. The anterior pair are called the nates, and the posterior the testes.
qualified: 1. Fitted by accomplishments or endowments. 2. Modified; limited; as, a qualified statement. Qualified fee (Law), a base fee, or an estate which has a qualification annexed to it, the fee ceasing with the qualification, as a grant to A and his heirs, tenants of the manor of Dale.
quizzism: The act or habit of quizzing.
quacksalver: One who boasts of his skill in medicines and salves, or of the efficacy of his prescriptions; a charlatan; a quack; a mountebank. (old) Burton.
quinquevalvular: Having five valves, as a pericarp.
quadriceps: The great extensor muscle of the knee, divided above into four parts which unite in a single tendon at the knee.
quadratrix: A curve made use of in the quadrature of other curves; as the quadratrix, of Dinostratus, or of Tschirnhausen.
quillback: An American fresh-water fish (Ictiobus, or Carpiodes, cyprinus); -- called also carp sucker, sailfish, spearfish, and skimback.
quinquevir: One of five commissioners appointed for some special object.
quieter: One who, or that which, quiets.
quasi: As if; as though; as it were; in a manner sense or degree; having some resemblance to; qualified; -- used as an adjective, or a prefix with a noun or an adjective; as, a quasi contract, an implied contract, an obligation which has arisen from some act, as if from a contract; a quasi corporation, a body that has some, but not all, of the peculiar attributes of a corporation;
quadrat: 1. (Print.) A block of type metal lower than the letters, -- used in spacing and in blank lines. [Abbrev. quad.] 2. An old instrument used for taking altitudes; -- called also geometrical square, and line of shadows.
quitch: 1. (Bot.) Same as Quitch grass. 2. Figuratively: A vice; a taint; an evil. To pick the vicious quitch Of blood and custom wholly out of him. Tennyson .
quartering: 1. (Naut.) Coming from a point well abaft the beam, but not directly astern; -- said of waves or any moving object. 2. (Mach.) At right angles, as the cranks of a locomotive, which are in planes… | 1. A station. (old) Bp. Montagu. 2. Assignment of quarters for soldiers; quarters. 3. (Her.) (a) The division of a shield containing different coats of arms into four or more compartments.
quadratojugal: (a) Of or pertaining to the quadrate and jugal bones. (b) Of or pertaining to the quadratojugal bone. -- n. The quadratojugal bone. Quadratojugal bone (Anat.), a bone at the base of the lower jaw in many animals.
quidnunc: One who is curious to know everything that passes; one who knows, or pretends to know, all that is going on. "The idle stories of quidnuncs." Motley.
quadragesimal: Belonging to Lent; used in Lent; Lenten.
quash: To abate, annul, overthrow, or make void; as, to quash an indictment. Blackstone. | 1. To beat down, or beat in pieces; to dash forcibly; to crush. The whales Against sharp rocks, like reeling vessels, quashed, Though huge as mountains, are in pieces dashed. Waller. 2. To crush;
quiddler: One who wastes his energy about trifles. Emerson.
quarl: A medusa, or jellyfish. The jellied quarl that flings At once a thousand streaming stings. J. R. Drake.
quicksighted: Having quick sight or acute discernment; quick to see or to discern. Locke. --Quick"-sight`ed*ness, n.
quadricornous: Having four horns, or hornlike organs; as, a quadricornous beetle.
quinazol: A complex nitrogenous base related to cinnoline. [Written also chinazol.]
quat: (a) A pustule. (old) (b) An annoying, worthless person. Shak. | To satiate; to satisfy. [Prov. Eng.]
quirkish: , Consisting of quirks; resembling a quirk. Barrow.
quid: A portion suitable to be chewed; a cud; as, a quid of tobacco. | To drop from the mouth, as food when partially chewed; -- said of horses. Youatt.
quarryfaced: Having a face left as it comes from the quarry and not smoothed with the chisel or point; -- said of stones.
quadrillion: According to the French notation, which is followed also upon the Continent and in the United States, a unit with fifteen ciphers annexed; according to the English notation, the number produced by involving a million to the fourth power, or the number represented by a unit with twenty-four ciphers annexed. See the Note under Numeration.
queachy: 1. Yielding or trembling under the feet, as moist or boggy ground; shaking; moving. "The queachy fens." "Godwin's queachy sands." Drayton. 2. Like a queach; thick; bushy. (old) Cockeram.
quaternity: 1. The number four. (old) Sir T. Browne. 2. The union of four in one, as of four persons; -- analogous to the theological term trinity.
quoth: Said; spoke; uttered; -- used only in the first and third persons in the past tenses, and always followed by its nominative, the word or words said being the object; as, quoth I. quoth he. "Let me not live, quoth he." Shak.
quinoline: A nitrogenous base, C9H7N obtained as a pungent colorless liquid by the distillation of alkaloids, bones, coal tar, etc. It the nucleus of many organic bodies, especially of certain alkaloids and related substances; hence, by extension, any one of the series of alkaloidal bases of which quinoline proper is the type. [Written also chinoline.]
quair: A quire; a book. (old) " The king's quhair." James I. (of Scotland).
quiddle: To spend time in trifling employments, or to attend to useful subjects in an indifferent or superficial manner; to dawdle. | One who wastes his energy about trifles. Emerson.
quietness: The quality or state of being quiet; freedom from noise, agitation, disturbance, or excitement; stillness; tranquillity; calmness. I would have peace and quietness. Shak.
quaternate: Composed of, or arranged in, sets of four; quaternary; as, quaternate leaves.
queenship: The state, rank, or dignity of a queen.
quadrisyllable: A word consisting of four syllables. De Quincey.
quadrature: 1. (Math.) The act of squaring; the finding of a square having the same area as some given curvilinear figure; as, the quadrature of a circle; the operation of finding an expression for the area of a figure bounded wholly or in part by a curved line, as by a curve, two ordinates, and the axis of abscissas. 2. A quadrate; a square. Milton. 3.
quicksilver: The metal mercury; -- so called from its resemblance to liquid silver. Quicksilver horizon, a mercurial artificial horizon. See under Horizon. -- Quicksilver water, a solution of mercury nitrate used in artificial silvering; quick water.
quintic: Of the fifth degree or order. -- n. (Alg.) A quantic of the fifth degree. See Quantic.
querist: One who inquires, or asks questions. Swift.
querl: To twirl; to turn or wind round; to coil; as, to querl a cord, thread, or rope. [Local, U.S.] | A coil; a twirl; as, the qwerl of hair on the fore leg of a blooded horse. [Local, U. S.]
quixotism: That form of delusion which leads to extravagant and absurd undertakings or sacrifices in obedience to a morbidly romantic ideal of duty or honor, as illustrated by the exploits of Don Quixote in knight-errantry.
quitchgrass: A perennial grass (Agropyrum repens) having long running rootstalks, by which it spreads rapidly and pertinaciously, and so becomes a troublesome weed. Also called couch grass, quick grass, quick grass, twitch grass. See Illustration in Appendix.
questor: An officer who had the management of the public treasure; a receiver of taxes, tribute, etc.; treasurer of state. [Written also quæstor.] Note: At an early period there were also public accusers styled questors, but the office was soon abolished.
quartine: A supposed fourth integument of an ovule, counting from the outside.
qualification: 1. The act of qualifying, or the condition of being qualified. 2. That which qualifies; any natural endowment, or any acquirement, which fits a person for a place, office, or employment, or which enables him to sustian any character with success; an enabling quality or circumstance; requisite capacity or possession.
qualifier: , One who, or that which, qualifies; that which modifies, reduces, tempers or restrains.
quindecemvirate: The body or office of the quindecemviri.
quarteron: A quarter; esp., a quarter of a pound, or a quarter of a hundred. Piers Plowman.
queenhood: The state, personality, or character of a queen; queenliness. Tennyson.
quartic: (a) (Alg.) A quantic of the fourth degree. See Quantic. (b) (Geom.) A curve or surface whose equation is of the fourth degree in the variables.
quiddany: A confection of quinces, in consistency between a sirup and marmalade.
quantity: 1. The attribute of being so much, and not more or less; the property of being measurable, or capable of increase and decrease, multiplication and division; greatness; and more concretely, that which answers the question "How much"; measure in regard to bulk or amount; determinate or comparative dimensions; measure; amount; bulk; extent; size.
quoddies: Herring taken and cured or smoked near Quoddy Head, Maine, or near the entrance of Passamaquoddy Ray.
quartet: 1. (Mus.) (a) A composition in four parts, each performed by a single voice or instrument. (b) The set of four person who perform a piece of music in four parts. 2. (Poet.) A stanza of four lines.
quarterfoil: An ornamental foliation having four lobes, or foils.
quicksilvered: Overlaid with quicksilver, or with an amalgam of quicksilver and tinfoil.
quickening: 1. The act or process of making or of becoming quick. 2. (Physiol.) The first motion of the fetus in the womb felt by the mother, occurring usually about the middle of the term of pregnancy. It has been popularly supposed to be due to the fetus becoming possessed of independent life.
quotum: Part or proportion; quota. "A very small quotum." Max Müller.
quirky: Full of quirks; tricky; as, a quirky lawyer.
quit: Any one of numerous species of small passerine birds native of tropical America. See Banana quit, under Banana, and Guitguit. | Released from obligation, charge, penalty, etc.; free; clear; absolved; acquitted. Chaucer. The owner of the ox shall be quit. Ex. xxi. 28. Note: This word is sometimes used in the form quits,…
quatre: A card, die. or domino, having four spots, or pips
questionable: 1. Admitting of being questioned; inviting, or seeming to invite, inquiry. Thou com'st in such a questionable shape That I will speak to thee. Shak. 2. Liable to question; subject to be doubted or called in question; problematical; doubtful; suspicious. It is questionable whether Galen ever saw the dissection of a human body.T. Baker. Syn. -- Disputable; debatable; uncertain;
quadrate: 1. Having four equal sides, the opposite sides parallel, and four right angles; square. Figures, some round, some triangle, some quadrate. Foxe. 2. Produced by multiplying a number by itself; square. | 1. (Geom.) A plane surface with four equal sides and four right angles; a square; hence, figuratively, anything having the outline of a square. At which command, the powers militant That stood for…
quaere: Inquire; question; see; -- used to signify doubt or to suggest investigation.
quaggy: Of the nature of a quagmire; yielding or trembling under the foot, as soft, wet earth; spongy; boggy. "O'er the watery strath, or quaggy moss." Collins.
queck: A word occurring in a corrupt passage of Bacon's Essays, and probably meaning, to stir, to move.
quadrilobate: Having four lobes; as, a quadrilobate leaf.
quadrifarious: Arranged in four rows or ranks; as, quadrifarious leaves. Loudon.
quaver: 1. To tremble; to vibrate; to shake. Sir I. Newton. 2. Especially, to shake the voice; to utter or form sound with rapid or tremulous vibrations, as in singing; also, to trill on a musical instrument | To utter with quavers. We shall hear her quavering them . . . to some sprightly airs of the opera. Addison.
quadragene: An indulgence of forty days, corresponding to the forty days of ancient canonical penance.
quercite: A white crystalline substance, C6H7(OH)5, found in acorns, the fruit of the oak (Quercus). It has a sweet taste, and is regarded as a pentacid alcohol.
quay: A mole, bank, or wharf, formed toward the sea, or at the side of a harbor, river, or other navigable water, for convenience in loading and unloading vessels. [Written also key.]
quadrilateral: Having four sides, and consequently four angles; quadrangular. | 1. (Geom.) A plane figure having four sides, and consequently four angles; a quadrangular figure; any figure formed by four lines. 2. An area defended by four fortresses supporting each other;
quadrable: That may be sqyared, or reduced to an equivalent square; -- said of a surface when the area limited by a curve can be exactly found, and expressed in a finite number of algebraic terms.
quadrangle: 1. (Geom.) A plane figure having four angles, and consequently four sides; any figure having four angles. 2. A square or quadrangular space or inclosure, such a space or court surrounded by buildings, esp. such a court in a college or public school in England.
quinizine: any one of a series of nitrogenous bases, certain of which are used as antipyretics.
querpo: The inner or body garments taken together. See Cuerpo. Dryden.
queenfish: A California sciænoid food fish (Seriphys politus). The back is bluish, and the sides and belly bright silvery. Called also kingfish.
quinquefoliated: Having five leaves or leaflets. Gray.
quassin: The bitter principle of quassia, extracted as a white crystalline substance; -- formerly called quassite. [Written also quassiin, and quassine.]
quondam: Having been formerly; former; sometime. "This is the quondam king." Shak. | A person dismissed or ejected from a position. "Make them quondams; . . . cast them out of their office." Latimer.
queest: The European ringdove (Columba palumbus); the cushat. [Written also quist, queeze, quice, queece.] See Ringdove.
quinizarin: A yellow crystalline substance produced artificially. It is isomeric with alizarin.
quint: 1. A set or sequence of five, as in piquet. 2. (Mus.) The interval of a fifth.
quartation: The act, process, or result (in the process of parting) of alloying a button of nearly pure gold with enough silver to reduce the fineness so as to allow acids to attack and remove all metals except the gold; -- called also inquartation. Compare Parting.
quintuplet: 1. A collection or combination of five of a kind. 2. pl. Five children born in the same labor. 3. (Mus.) A group of five connected notes; a turn of five notes. 4. A cycle having five crank shafts and adapted for five riders, all of whom can assist in the propulsion.
quadrisyllabical: Having four syllables; of or pertaining to quadrisyllables; as, a quadrisyllabic word.
questioner: One who asks questions; an inquirer. "Little time for idle questioners." Tennyson.
quicklime: Calcium oxide; unslacked lime; -- so called because when wet it develops great heat. See 4th Lime, 2.
query: 1. A question; an inquiry to be answered or solved. I shall conclude with proposing only some queries, in order to a . . . search to be made by others. Sir I. Newton. 2. A question in the mind; | 1. To ask questions; to make inquiry. Each prompt to query, answer, and debate. Pope. 2. To have a doubt; as, I query if he is right.
quotha: Indeed; forsooth. To affront the blessed hillside drabs and thieves With mended morals, quotha, -- fine new lives ! Mrs. Browning.
quaternion: 1. The number four. (poetic) 2. A set of four parts, things, or person; four things taken collectively; a group of four words, phrases, circumstances, facts, or the like. | To divide into quaternions, files, or companies. Milton.
quadrifoil: Four-leaved; having the leaves in whorls of four.
quaffer: One who quaffs, or drinks largely.
quench: 1. To extinguish; to overwhelm; to make an end of; -- said of flame and fire, of things burning, and figuratively of sensations and emotions; as, to quench flame; to quench a candle; | To become extinguished; to go out; to become calm or cool. Dost thou think in time She will not quench! Shak.
quinoa: The seeds of a kind of goosewort (Chenopodium Quinoa), used in Chili and Peru for making porridge or cakes; also, food thus made.
queint: imp. & p. p. of Quench. Chaucer.
quant: A punting pole with a broad flange near the end to prevent it from sinking into the mud; a setting pole.
quintain: An object to be tilted at; -- called also quintel. [Written also quintin.] Note: A common form in the Middle Ages was an upright post, on the top of which turned a crosspiece, having on one end a broad board, and on the other a sand bag. The endeavor was to strike the board with the lance while riding under, and get away without being hit by the sand bag.
querimonious: Complaining; querulous; apt to complain. -- Quer`i*mo"ni*ous*ly, adv. -- Quer`i*mo"ni*ous*ness, n.
quantification: Modification by a reference to quantity; the introduction of the element of quantity. The quantification of the predicate belongs in part to Sir William Hamilton; viz., in its extension to negative propositions. De Quincey.
quiescency: The state or quality of being quiescent. "Quiescence, bodily and mental." H. Spencer. Deeds will be done; -- while be boasts his quiescence. R. Browning.
quade: Evil; bad; baffling; as, a quade wind. (old) Sooth play, quad play, as the Fleming saith. Chaucer.
quakerish: Like or pertaining to a Quaker; Quakerlike.
quadruplex: Fourfold; folded or doubled twice. Quadruplex system (Electric Telegraph), a system by which four messages, two in each direction, may be sent simultaneously over the wire.
quadruplane: An aëroplane with four superposed main supporting surfaces.
quercitrin: A glucoside extracted from the bark of the oak (Quercus) as a bitter citron-yellow crystalline substance, used as a pigment and called quercitron.
quartersaw: To saw (a log) into quarters; specif., to saw into quarters and then into boards, as by cutting alternately from each face of a quarter, to secure lumber that will warp relatively little or show the grain advantageously.
quadriga: A car or chariot drawn by four horses abreast.
quodlibetarian: One who discusses any subject at pleasure.
quinquepartite: 1. Consisting of five parts. 2. (Bot.) Divided into five parts almost to the base.
quincuncially: In the manner or order of a quincunx.
quandong: The edible drupaceous fruit of an Australian tree (Fusanus acuminatus) of the Sandalwood family; -- called also quandang.
quotable: Capable or worthy of being quoted; as, a quotable writer; a quotable sentence. -- Quot`a*bit"i*ty, n. Poe.
quixotic: Like Don Quixote; romantic to extravagance; absurdly chivalric; apt to be deluded. "Feats of quixotic gallantry." Prescott.
quadrel: 1. A square piece of turf or peat. [Prov. Eng.] 2. A square brick, tile, or the like.
quillet: Subtilty; nicety; quibble. "Nice, sharp quillets of the law." Shak.
quadrangular: Having four angles, and consequently four sides; tetragonal. -- Quad*ran"gu*lar*ly, adv.
quenchless: Incapable of being quenched; inextinguishable; as, quenchless fire or fury. "Once kindled, quenchless evermore." Byron. Syn. -- Inextinguishable; unquenchable. -- Quench"less*ly, adv. -- Quench"less*ness, n.
quotationist: One who makes, or is given to making, quotations. The narrow intellectuals of quotationists. Milton.
querken: To stifle or choke. [Prov. Eng.] Halliwell.
queenliness: The quality of being queenly; the; characteristic of a queen; stateliness; eminence among women in attractions or power.
queendom: The dominion, condition, or character of a queen. Mrs. Browning.
quiddit: A subtilty; an equivocation. (old) Shak. By some strange quiddit or some wrested clause. Drayton.
querulous: 1. Given to quarreling; quarrelsome. (old) land. 2. Apt to find fault; habitually complaining; disposed to murmur; as, a querulous man or people. Enmity can hardly be more annoying that querulous, jealous, exacting fondness. Macaulay. 3. Expressing complaint; fretful; whining; as, a querulous tone of voice. Syn. -- Complaining; bewailing; lamenting; whining; mourning;
quinhydrone: A green crystalline substance formed by the union of quinone with hydroquinone, or as an intermediate product in the oxidation of hydroquinone or the reduction of quinone. [Written also chinhydrone.]
quinoyl: A radical of which quinone is the hydride, analogous to phenyl. [Written also kinoyl.]
quaint: 1. Prudent; wise; hence, crafty; artful; wily. (old) Clerks be full subtle and full quaint. Chaucer. 2. Characterized by ingenuity or art; finely fashioned; skillfully wrought; elegant; graceful; nice; neat. (old) " The queynte ring." " His queynte spear." Chaucer. " A shepherd young quaint." Chapman. Every look was coy and wondrous quaint. Spenser.
quaff: To drink with relish; to drink copiously of; to swallow in large draughts. "Quaffed off the muscadel." Shak. They eat, they drink, and in communion sweet Quaff immortality and joy. Milton. | To drink largely or luxuriously. Twelve days the gods their solemn revels keep, And quaff with blameless Ethiops in the deep. Dryden.
quietistic: Of or pertaining to the Quietists, or to Quietism.
quadripennate: Having four wings; -- said of insects.
quilter: One who, or that which, quilts.
quantitative: Relating to quantity. -- Quan"ti*ta*tive*ly, adv. Quantitative analysis (Chem.), analysis which determines the amount or quantity of each ingredient of a substance, by weight or by volume; -- contrasted with qualitative analysis.
qualm: 1. Sickness; disease; pestilence; death. (old) thousand slain and not of qualm ystorve [dead]. Chaucer. 2. A sudden attack of illness, faintness, or pain; an agony. " Qualms of heartsick agony." Milton. 3. Especially, a sudden sensation of nausea. For who, without a qualm, hath ever looked On holy garbage, though by Homer cooked Roscommon. 4. A prick or scruple of conscience;
quakerism: The peculiar character, manners, tenets, etc., of the Quakers.
quassia: The wood of several tropical American trees of the order Simarubeæ, as Quassia amara, Picræna excelsa, and Simaruba amara. It is intensely bitter, and is used in medicine and sometimes as a substitute for hops in making beer.
quarryman: A man who is engaged in quarrying stones; a quarrier.
quickstep: A lively, spirited march; also, a lively style of dancing.
quadridentate: Having four teeth; as, a quadridentate leaf.
quicksand: Sand easily moved or readily yielding to pressure; especially, a deep mass of loose or moving sand mixed with water, sometimes found at the mouth of a river or along some coasts, and very dangerous, from the difficulty of extricating a person who begins sinking into it. Life hath quicksands, -- Life hath snares! Longfellow.
quintole: A group of five notes to be played or sung in the time of four of the same species.
quantic: A homogeneous algebraic function of two or more variables, in general containing only positive integral powers of the variables, and called quadric, cubic, quartic, etc., according as it is of the second, third, fourth, fifth, or a higher degree. These are further called binary, ternary, quaternary, etc., according as they contain two, three, four, or more variables;
quencher: One who, or that which, quenches. Hammond.
quartzite: Massive quartz occurring as a rock; a metamorphosed sandstone; -- called also quartz rock.
quadrilobed: Having four lobes; as, a quadrilobate leaf.
queentruss: A truss framed with queen-posts; a queen-post truss.
queen: 1. The wife of a king. 2. A woman who is the sovereign of a kingdom; a female monarch; as, Elizabeth, queen of England; Mary, queen of Scots. In faith, and by the heaven's quene. Chaucer. 3. | To act the part of a queen. Shak.
quinate: Growing in sets of five; -- said especially of leaves composed of five leaflets set at the end of a common petiole. | A salt of quinic acid. [Written also kinate.]
quiet: 1. In a state of rest or calm; without stir, motion, or agitation; still; as, a quiet sea; quiet air.
